g.text: -> Path based:
+ Easy to set up and maintain, suitable for standard directory structures.
- Insecure if attackers can place malicious files in allowed directories.
-> Hash-based:
+ very secure, as only files with the exact approved hash can run.
- Every software update changes the has - high maintenance effort.
-> Certificate-based
+ Easier for updates, as all binaries signed by the trusted publisher are
allowed automatically.
- Requires full trust in the publisher; if the certificate is compromised,
all signed malware may run.
To log which applications would be blocked without actually blocking them. its
purpose to test and fine-tune a whitelist before enforcing it.

g.text: then with a token
An ACL is a list that defines which users or systems (identified by their SIDs) have what kind of access to
specific resources. Each entry in an ACL is called an ACE and specifies the SID and the type of access
allowed or denied.
A token contains a collection of SIDs that represent the security context of a user or a process. When a user
logs in, they receive a token that includes their SIDs and the privilege they have.
- SeTakeOwnershipsPrivilege: allows to take ownerships and override ACL permissions
- SeRestorePrivilege: This privilege allows user to override file and folder ACLs when restoring files and
folders from backup
